name: Common Lodge
tagline: A green container café-lodge under one south-facing shed roof.
description: Three reused 40-foot containers in deep green, with yellow-framed glazing and a tall glazed central hall, frame a community lodge beside the water. One gable roof with a clear ridge covers the whole building; the solar array is mounted only on the south slope and is aligned to true south independently of the building. The north wing holds the shared kitchen, pantry, laundry and accessible washrooms; the central hall is the shared dining and gathering space; the south wing holds the workshop, meeting room and boot room; the west wing holds the café servery, office and a universal washroom. A screened veranda and covered entrance connect the hall to the forest. The existing authoritative lodge model is preserved separately; this is an additional Design Lab concept.

foundation.type: Engineered helical piles with adjustable brackets
foundation.frost_design: Engineered pile depth and uplift resistance below frost; geotechnical review required.
foundation.ground_disturbance: Point loads only; no slab, fill or grade change. Use matting, root protection and a construction sequence reviewed by an arborist.
foundation.note: Elevated floor on engineered helical piles. Confirm soil, bedrock, frost uplift, corrosion, lateral capacity, slope stability and permit requirements before construction.

thermal.wall_insulation_strategy: continuous external wood-fibre board + mineral wool (200 mm) with thermal breaks and a ventilated rainscreen
thermal.thermal_bridge_mitigation: continuous external insulation with thermal washers and stainless fasteners; breaks at openings, pile caps and service penetrations
thermal.air_vapour_control: exterior-insulated, vapour-open assembly; sealed interior air barrier (to be detailed)
thermal.window_performance: triple glazed, low-e, argon, thermally broken frames
thermal.external_shading: fixed overhang, covered veranda and deciduous planting
thermal.notes: Conceptual thermal intent only. Large glazed hall needs condensation, solar gain and insulated door review. No energy or code calculation.

features.outdoor: 8.0 × 3.0 m screened veranda, covered west entrance, decks
features.solar: A single 39° south-facing array on the south slope of a 10° gable roof; no north-side array. True south, independent of building rotation.
features.green_roof: Green/solar roof on the north module; weight, drainage and fire review required
features.accessibility: Step-free hall and veranda intended; two accessible washrooms, one with an adult-size change table; door widths, turning spaces and counter heights need verification.
features.environment: Three reused green containers and a glazed timber hall share one gable roof; only the south slope carries solar. Large glazing and a green roof increase the technical review.

status: concept only; not reviewed; not for construction

envelope.thermal_breaks: continuous external insulation with thermal washers and stainless fasteners; breaks at openings, pile caps and service penetrations
envelope.air_vapour_control: exterior-insulated, vapour-open assembly with a sealed interior air barrier; joints and service penetrations to be detailed
envelope.fire: combustible insulation, cladding and cavity need a fire review; cavity barriers, cladding classification and separation are not resolved
envelope.fastening: long fasteners pass through the insulation into the steel frame; pull-out, corrosion, thermal bridging and water shedding need engineering review
envelope.penetrations: openings, cladding rails, planter brackets and service penetrations need structural and waterproofing review
envelope.maintenance: inspect cladding, sealant, cavity, fasteners and vegetation twice a year and after severe weather
envelope.notes: The hybrid combines vapour-open wood fibre with mineral wool; the large glazed hall and green roof add envelope complexity.

solar_array.mounting: tilted racks on the 10° south gable slope; panels at 39° from horizontal

solar_array.note: Array is aligned to true south regardless of building rotation; it sits only on the south roof slope. Snow shedding, wind uplift, roof structure and electrical design need review.
